## Purpose

This SOP describes the preparation of amplicon sequencing libraries for
Illumina platforms, following a two-step PCR approach. The first PCR
amplifies the target marker gene (e.g., 16S rRNA for bacteria, ITS for
fungi) with gene-specific primers tailed with Illumina adapter
overhangs. The second PCR attaches unique dual-index barcodes and the
full Illumina adapter sequences, enabling multiplexed sequencing of many
samples per run. This protocol is based on the Illumina 16S Metagenomic
Sequencing Library Preparation guide and the Earth Microbiome Project
(EMP) standards [@caporaso2012; @illumina_16s_2013; @thompson2017].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Preparation of amplicon libraries targeting 16S rRNA
  (V4 or V3--V4 region), ITS (ITS1 or ITS2 region), 18S rRNA, or other
  marker genes from environmental DNA extracts for paired-end sequencing
  on Illumina MiSeq or NextSeq platforms
- **Does not apply to:** Shotgun metagenomic library preparation; long-
  read amplicon sequencing (PacBio, Nanopore); ddPCR (see
  [SOP-L701](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd)); eDNA
  metabarcoding using non-Illumina workflows
- **Location:** Molecular biology bench, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve target region, primer choice, and sequencing facility |
| Trained Personnel | Prepare libraries per this SOP; submit to sequencing facility |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** AMPure XP beads (or equivalent SPRI beads) contain
  polyethylene glycol (PEG) and carboxylated magnetic particles; low
  toxicity but handle with gloves. Molecular-grade ethanol is flammable.
- **Biological:** Environmental DNA extracts may contain pathogen-derived
  DNA. Handle with standard precautions.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (changed frequently)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

| Qubit 4 fluorometer              | Instrument bench | For library quantification     |
| NanoDrop One                      | Instrument bench | Optional purity check          |
| Gel electrophoresis system        | Mol bio bench    | For amplicon verification; see [SOP-L703](SOP-L703-pcr-gel-electrophoresis.qmd) |

| Plate vortex mixer                | Mol bio bench    | For mixing bead suspensions    |

### Reagents and Consumables

| Item                                  | Notes                              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| High-fidelity DNA polymerase          | e.g., KAPA HiFi HotStart (Roche), Q5 (NEB), or Phusion (Thermo Fisher); high-fidelity polymerase is required to minimize PCR-introduced errors [@schirmer2015] |
| Gene-specific primers with Illumina overhangs (PCR1) | See Section 6.1 |
| Nextera XT Index Kit v2 (or equivalent dual-index primers) | For PCR2 barcoding |
| AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter) or equivalent SPRI beads | For size selection and cleanup |
| Molecular-grade ethanol (80%, freshly prepared) | For bead washes |
| Nuclease-free water                   | For elution and dilutions          |
| Qubit dsDNA HS Assay Kit              | For library quantification         |
| Agarose and gel supplies              | For amplicon verification          |
| PCR plates or strip tubes (0.2 mL)    | Low-bind preferred                 |
| Plate sealing film or strip caps      |                                    |
| Filter pipette tips                   | Barrier tips mandatory             |


## Procedure

### Primer Design (PCR1: Gene-Specific Amplification)

Primers for the first PCR consist of the gene-specific sequence plus
the Illumina adapter overhang. The overhang sequences are:

- Forward overhang:
  `5'-TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG-[gene-specific forward]-3'`
- Reverse overhang:
  `5'-GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG-[gene-specific reverse]-3'`

**Commonly used gene-specific primers:**

| Target          | Primers        | Region  | Amplicon | Reference         |
|:----------------|:---------------|:--------|:---------|:------------------|
| 16S bacteria/archaea | 515F / 806R | V4      | ~290 bp  | @caporaso2012; @parada2016 |
| 16S bacteria    | 341F / 785R    | V3--V4  | ~460 bp  | @klindworth2013   |
| ITS fungi       | ITS1f / ITS2   | ITS1    | ~250--400 bp | @smith2009; @white1990 |
| ITS fungi       | fITS7 / ITS4   | ITS2    | ~250--400 bp | @ihrmark2012      |
| 18S eukaryotes  | Euk1391f / EukBr | V9    | ~130 bp  | @amaralzettler2009 |

::: {.callout-note}
The EMP standard primers for 16S V4 are 515F (Parada) / 806R (Apprill),
which include degeneracies for improved archaeal coverage
[@parada2016; @apprill2015]. Use these unless the project specifically
requires a different region.
:::

### PCR1: Target Amplification

1. Prepare the master mix on ice. Use a high-fidelity polymerase.

| Component                    | Volume per reaction | Final concentration |
|:-----------------------------|:--------------------|:--------------------|
| 2x KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix | 12.5 uL         | 1x                  |
| Forward primer with overhang (10 uM) | 1.0 uL   | 400 nM              |
| Reverse primer with overhang (10 uM) | 1.0 uL   | 400 nM              |
| Nuclease-free water          | 8.5 uL              | --                  |
| Template DNA (1--10 ng)      | 2.0 uL              | Variable            |
| **Total**                    | **25.0 uL**         |                     |

2. Include controls: positive control, NTC, and extraction blank.
3. Cycling parameters (adjust annealing temperature per primer set):

| Step                   | Temperature | Time   | Cycles |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:-------|:-------|
| Initial denaturation   | 95 C        | 3 min  | 1      |
| Denaturation           | 95 C        | 30 s   | 25--28 |
| Annealing              | 55 C        | 30 s   | 25--28 |
| Extension              | 72 C        | 30 s   | 25--28 |
| Final extension        | 72 C        | 5 min  | 1      |
| Hold                   | 4 C         | Hold   | --     |

::: {.callout-important}
Limit PCR1 to 25--28 cycles to minimize chimera formation and PCR bias
[@schirmer2015]. More cycles increase the proportion of artifacts in the
sequencing data.
:::

4. Verify amplification by running 2 uL on a 1.5% agarose gel per
   [SOP-L703](SOP-L703-pcr-gel-electrophoresis.qmd).

### PCR1 Cleanup (SPRI Beads)

1. Allow AMPure XP beads to reach room temperature (approximately
   30 minutes). Vortex well before use.
2. Add 20 uL (0.8x ratio) of beads to each 25 uL PCR product. Mix by
   pipetting 10 times.
3. Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
4. Place on the magnetic stand for 2 minutes until the solution clears.
5. Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
6. Wash twice with 200 uL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol. Do not
   disturb the bead pellet. Allow 30 seconds per wash.
7. Remove all ethanol and air-dry the beads for 3--5 minutes. Do not
   over-dry (beads will crack and yield drops).
8. Remove from the magnetic stand. Elute in 27.5 uL of nuclease-free
   water. Pipette to mix.
9. Return to the magnetic stand. Transfer 25 uL of the clear eluate to
   a new tube.

### PCR2: Index PCR (Barcoding)

1. Assign a unique dual-index combination (i7 + i5) to each sample.
   Record the plate map in the lab notebook and in the sample sheet.
2. Set up the index PCR:

| Component                    | Volume per reaction |
|:-----------------------------|:--------------------|
| 2x KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix | 12.5 uL         |
| Nextera XT Index Primer 1 (i7) | 2.5 uL           |
| Nextera XT Index Primer 2 (i5) | 2.5 uL           |
| Cleaned PCR1 product         | 2.5 uL              |
| Nuclease-free water          | 5.0 uL              |
| **Total**                    | **25.0 uL**         |

3. Cycling parameters:

| Step                   | Temperature | Time   | Cycles |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:-------|:-------|
| Initial denaturation   | 95 C        | 3 min  | 1      |
| Denaturation           | 95 C        | 30 s   | 8      |
| Annealing              | 55 C        | 30 s   | 8      |
| Extension              | 72 C        | 30 s   | 8      |
| Final extension        | 72 C        | 5 min  | 1      |
| Hold                   | 4 C         | Hold   | --     |

4. Clean the indexed PCR product with AMPure XP beads (0.8x ratio)
   as in Section 6.3. Elute in 27.5 uL.

### Library Quantification and QC

1. Quantify each library using the Qubit dsDNA HS Assay
   ([SOP-L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd), Section 6.4).
2. Verify library size by running 1 uL on a 1.5% agarose gel. The
   expected size is the amplicon plus approximately 120 bp of adapter
   and index sequence.
3. Libraries with concentrations below 1 nM may not sequence well.
   Re-amplify or exclude them.

### Library Pooling and Submission

1. Normalize each library to an equimolar concentration (typically
   4 nM) by diluting with nuclease-free water.
2. Pool equal volumes of all normalized libraries into a single tube.
3. Quantify the pooled library by Qubit.
4. Prepare the sample sheet (Illumina Experiment Manager format or
   the sequencing facility's template) listing every sample with its
   index combination.
5. Submit the pooled library and sample sheet to the sequencing
   facility per their submission guidelines.
6. Record the submission date, facility, run type (e.g., MiSeq 2x250
   or 2x300), and expected turnaround in the lab notebook.


## Quality Control

- Every library prep run must include: positive control (mock
  community, if available), NTC, and extraction blank carried through
  both PCR1 and PCR2
- NTC and extraction blanks must show no visible band on the
  verification gel and no detectable concentration on the Qubit. If
  blanks are positive, the entire batch is suspect [@salter2014].
- Verify amplicon size on gel after PCR1; verify library size (amplicon
  + adapters) on gel after PCR2
- Record the number of PCR1 cycles and the index assignments for every
  sample; these are required for data analysis and troubleshooting


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Container                 | Disposal Method                     |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------|:------------------------------------|
| Used SPRI beads               | Standard trash            | Non-hazardous                       |
| Ethanol wash waste            | Chemical waste or evaporate in fume hood | Small volumes can evaporate |
| Used PCR tubes, plates, tips  | Standard trash            | Non-hazardous                       |
| Gel waste                     | Per [SOP-L703](SOP-L703-pcr-gel-electrophoresis.qmd) | Depends on stain used |

## Training Record

Before preparing amplicon libraries independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-L703](SOP-L703-pcr-gel-electrophoresis.qmd), and
   [SOP-L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate SPRI bead cleanup with correct bead ratios and wash steps
3. Prepare a supervised library from positive control DNA through pooling,
   with clean controls and correct library size on gel
4. Complete the sequencing facility's sample submission training
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
